findings.place: section 4.3 mode `with-child` and section 11.1 E2S-13; section 16 S02 ('applied (F36)')
findings.what: The rework claims S02 (no SIGKILL to the group after the main process ended) is caught by E2S-13 because the child of `with-child` ignores SIGTERM. The text makes the child the same script started with `--child`, which 'writes no event', and the parent 'logs its pid' at once. A Node child needs about 40 ms to install its SIGTERM handler; E2S-13 as worded starts the stand, reads the logged child pid, calls `stop()`. The group SIGTERM then reaches the child before its handler exists and kills it, so there is nothing for the final SIGKILL to do. I built the starter, the stand-in and the test from the text: S02 survives 6 of 6 runs (c13 ok, stop() resolves, child gone). With a 400 ms wait before `stop()` S02 is red 3 of 3 (`CLEANUP_FAILED ... group still alive`, the child stays alive; I killed those children by pid). The sketch s16 of the designer had a 300 ms wait and an inline child (`node -e` with the handler in its first statement); neither the wait nor the readiness is in the text, and the `--child` form of 4.3 was not run by the designer. As written, S02 is not closed and the developer would have to invent the synchronisation.
findings.needed: Specify the readiness of the child: the child (not the parent) tells the test that it ignores SIGTERM now (an event written after the handler is installed, or the parent prints the link only after the child said so), and E2S-13 waits for that signal (with a limit) before `stop()`. Update 4.3 ('writes no event' is the sentence in the way) and E2S-13; then S02 can be called applied only after a run of that form (run it at least 3 times).
